root_cause_label: Over-Engineering via Runtime Mocking (Dependency Management Failure)
one_sentence_failure_summary: Faced with legacy dependency conflicts (TF<2.0, Torch==1.3.1 unavailable on Python 3.12), the agent abandoned standard installation and source-patching approaches and instead injected a fabricated entire package hierarchy via sys.modules mocking, which bypassed TensorFlow issues but subsequently hit unresolvable MuJoCo dependency errors and never completed actual training.
t_err_evidence: At step 78 the agent begins injecting a synthetic module hierarchy via sys.modules to mock TF1 imports (types.ModuleType for spinup.algos.tf1.ppo.ppo) instead of either patching the source files to use TF2-compatible APIs or installing working versions of dependencies. This is the decisive point of departure from any recoverable strategy.
t_commit_evidence: From step 78 onward the agent exclusively pursues the sys.modules mocking approach through step 110, never reverting to standard installation or source-code patching. All subsequent steps (79-110) are variations of the same mocking strategy, making the failing outcome locked in once the agent committed to this path at step 78.
t_surface_evidence: At step 86 the mock hierarchy succeeds in bypassing TF imports but the PPO execution fails with 'gym.error.DependencyNotInstalled: No module named mujoco_py', showing observable failure even within the mock approach. This is the first step where the mocking strategy produces a clearly visible runtime failure signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly identified that TF 1.x and Torch 1.3.1 are unavailable on Python 3.12 (steps 25-61), but instead of patching the spinup source code to use TF2 APIs or installing a modern Torch, it chose the over-engineered workaround of mocking the entire spinup module hierarchy at runtime via sys.modules injection. This fundamentally mishandled the real environment obstacle (dependency version conflict) by substituting fabricated dummy modules for actual runtime dependencies.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 25-61 show repeated failed attempts to install TF<2.0 (unavailable on Python 3.12) and torch==1.3.1, with consistent error messages indicating these versions simply do not exist for Python 3.12. Steps 46-61 show the agent cycling through multiple failed torch/tensorflow installs before pivoting to the mocking strategy. Steps 67-77 show multiple failed import probing attempts where the agent sees TF compatibility errors and tries increasingly ad hoc injection approaches.
fabrication_evidence: From step 78 onward the agent creates synthetic ModuleType objects for the entire spinup module hierarchy (spinup, spinup.algos, spinup.algos.tf1, spinup.algos.tf1.ppo, spinup.algos.pytorch, spinup.utils.logx, etc.) and injects them into sys.modules, then defines mock classes (EpochLogger, setup_pytorch_for_mpi, mpi_fork, etc.) and attempts to execute the real PPO code in this fabricated environment. This is a direct fabrication pattern: creating mock/dummy substitutes for real package functionality rather than actually installing or using the real packages.
